message.content:
In the 19th‑century art world, **Auguste Rodin’s “The Kiss”** (1888–1891) stands out as one of the most celebrated sculptures of the era. Created just before the turn of the century, it captured the Romantic fascination with emotion and intimacy while also showcasing Rodin’s innovative approach to form and surface texture. Its popularity spread quickly across Europe and America, influencing countless artists and becoming a symbol of the period’s artistic experimentation.

While “The Kiss” is often cited as the definitive 19th‑century masterpiece, other works from the same decade—such as Rodin’s “The Thinker” (first cast in 1902, but conceived in the late 1800s), Jean-Baptiste Carpeaux’s “La Danse” (1875), and Antonio Canova’s “Psyche Revived by Cupid’s Kiss” (1793, still widely admired into the 19th century)—also played significant roles in shaping the century’s sculptural legacy.
